name: Cat in the Sack: Two-Stage Auction
summary: Each round every player secretly adds one card to a shared sack, then everyone bids mice in two simultaneous sealed stages for a sack whose cards are only partly revealed. Final score is cat points plus mice.

player.meaning: The player's private cards. Setup moves one card out at random, leaving 9.
The card this player put into this round's sack.
The player's money for bidding. It is part of the final score.
The sum of the sack values this player has won. It can be negative.
The number this player wrote in the current stage. It is announced after each stage.
The player's effective bid in stage 2. It is 0 if the player has none.
Whether the player is still bidding this round.

game.meaning: The face-down pile holding the card removed from each hand at setup.
The start player. That player's card is sack card 1.
The seats in sack order: start_seat first, then upward, wrapping to seat 1.
Each owner's played_card, in sack_owners order.
The sack cards revealed so far this round.
Sack cards discarded after each round.
The highest stage-1 bid when two or more players bid.
The seat holding the standing_bid after stage 1. It is 0 if there is none.
How many players bid more than 0 in stage 1.
True when the round's sack is settled: nobody bid, or it has been taken.
The seat that wins the sack this round. It is 0 if there is none.
The mice the sack winner pays.
The value of the sack won this round, after the dog rule.

setup: Every player receives the same 10 cards: cat_-8, cat_-5, cat_3, cat_5, cat_8, cat_11, cat_15, rabbit, large_dog and small_dog.
One random card is removed from each player's hand and appended to the hidden table list set_aside, so each hand holds 9 private cards.
Each player's mice is set to 15 and cat_points to 0. Both are public.
start_seat is chosen at random from the seats. This is the only time it is randomised.
round_number is set to 0. The game lasts 9 rounds.

round.effect: For every player, set bid=0, effective_bid=0 and in_auction=true. Set standing_bid=0, leader_seat=0, bidder_count=0, sack_done=false, sack_winner=0, winning_bid=0 and sack_value=0. Set sack_cards=[] and sack_revealed=[].

round.answer: one card from the player's own hand
round.effect: The chosen card is removed from that player's hand and stored as their played_card, which is private.

Set sack_owners to all seats in order, starting at start_seat and counting upward, wrapping from the last seat to seat 1. Set sack_cards to each owner's played_card in that same order. Announce sack_owners to everyone.
No state change. Broadcast to all: "Seat {seat} says: {value}". Talk is not binding.
Stage 1: reveal sack_cards[1] (the start player's card) by appending it to sack_revealed, and announce it. standing_bid stays 0.

round.answer: a whole number from 0 to the player's mice
round.effect: Store the number as that player's bid.

Announce every bid by seat. For each player with bid=0 or bid>mice: mice += 2 and in_auction=false. Set bidder_count = the number of players with in_auction=true. If bidder_count=0: sack_done=true and start_seat = (start_seat mod N) + 1. If bidder_count=1: sack_winner = that seat and winning_bid = that player's bid. If bidder_count>=2: standing_bid = the highest bid, and leader_seat = the seat with that bid; on a tie, the tied seat with the smallest (seat - start_seat - 1 + N) mod N.
When bidder_count>=2 (stage 2): reveal sack_cards[2] by appending it to sack_revealed, and announce it.

round.who: each player with in_auction=true, when bidder_count>=2
round.answer: 0, or a whole number from standing_bid+1 to the player's mice
round.effect: Store the number as that player's bid.

When bidder_count>=2: announce every stage-2 number by seat. For the leader, effective_bid = standing_bid if bid=0, else bid. For any other in_auction player, effective_bid = bid if standing_bid < bid <= mice, else 0. sack_winner = the seat with the highest effective_bid. On a tie, the leader wins if tied; otherwise the tied seat with the smallest (seat - start_seat - 1 + N) mod N wins. winning_bid = the winner's effective_bid. Every other player with in_auction=true gets mice += 3.

When sack_winner != 0 (taking the sack): the winner pays mice -= winning_bid. Reveal all of sack_cards by setting sack_revealed = sack_cards. Dog rule, only when exactly one of large_dog and small_dog is in sack_cards. Large dog: remove the highest positive cat, or the most negative cat if there is no positive cat. Small dog: remove the most negative cat, or the lowest positive cat if there is no negative cat. No cat: nothing happens. sack_value = the sum of the remaining cat values (rabbit and dogs count 0). The winner gets cat_points += sack_value. Set start_seat = sack_winner and sack_done = true.
Append all of sack_cards to discard_pile and set sack_cards=[]. round_number += 1. Announce mice and cat_points for every seat.
Each player is sent their own state (hand, mice, cat_points).
If round_number >= 9 the game ends; otherwise the next round begins.

ending.decided_by: Each player's score is cat_points + mice, and the highest score wins. Among tied players, more cat_points wins. Players still tied share the win (a draw).

rules.text: At setup each player holds the 10 cards cat_-8, cat_-5, cat_3, cat_5, cat_8, cat_11, cat_15, rabbit, large_dog and small_dog. One random card from each hand then moves to the hidden set_aside list, leaving 9 cards in each hand.
At setup each player has mice=15 and cat_points=0, both public. start_seat is chosen at random once, and the game lasts 9 rounds.

At the start of each round every player has bid=0 and in_auction=true, and standing_bid=0, leader_seat=0, sack_done=false and sack_winner=0. Each player then simultaneously moves one card from their hand to played_card, so the hand shrinks by 1.
sack_owners lists every seat starting at start_seat, ascending and wrapping, and sack_cards holds each owner's played_card in that order. With start_seat=3 of 4, sack_owners=[3,4,1,2].
Before stage 1, every player simultaneously sends one short message, and all messages are then shown with seat names.
In stage 1, sack_cards[1] is appended to sack_revealed, and each player simultaneously picks a bid from 0 to their mice. A bid of 0 is a pass.
When a player passes in stage 1 (bid 0, or bid above their mice), that player gains 2 mice and gets in_auction=false.
When nobody bids in stage 1, nobody takes the sack, the sack cards are discarded and start_seat becomes (start_seat mod N)+1. With N=4 and start_seat=4, start_seat becomes 1.
When exactly one player bids in stage 1, that player wins the sack at their bid, and stage 2 does not happen.
When two or more players bid in stage 1, standing_bid is the highest bid and leader_seat is its bidder. A tie goes to the first tied seat counting from the seat after start_seat.
In stage 2, sack_cards[2] is revealed, and each player with in_auction=true is offered 0 or any whole number from standing_bid+1 to their mice.
When the leader answers 0 in stage 2, their effective bid equals standing_bid. When the leader answers a number above standing_bid, that number is their effective bid.
When a non-leader answers 0, or a number not above standing_bid or above their mice, in stage 2, that player has no effective bid.
In stage 2 the highest effective bid wins. On a tie the leader wins if among the tied players; otherwise the first tied seat counting from the seat after start_seat wins.
When stage 2 resolves, every in_auction player other than the winner gains 3 mice.
The sack winner pays winning_bid mice, all sack cards are revealed, and the winner becomes start_seat.

When exactly one dog is in the sack and it is large_dog, it removes the highest positive cat, or the most negative cat if there is no positive cat. Example: a sack of cat_15, cat_3, large_dog has value 3.

When exactly one dog is in the sack and it is small_dog, it removes the most negative cat, or the lowest positive cat if there is no negative cat. Example: a sack of cat_-8, cat_5, small_dog has value 5.
When the sack holds zero or two dogs, no cat is removed. Example: a sack of cat_15, large_dog, small_dog has value 15.
sack_value is the sum of the remaining cat values, with rabbit and dogs worth 0, and it is added to the winner's cat_points even if negative. Example: cat_-8, rabbit, cat_-5 gives -13.
After round 9 the game ends, and the highest cat_points+mice wins. Ties go to more cat_points, and a remaining tie is a shared win.

offers.question: Play a card into the sack
offers.options: Each card currently in that player's own hand (9 cards in round 1, falling by one each round).

offers.question: Stage 1 bid
offers.options: Every whole number from 0 to the player's current mice (0 = pass).

offers.question: Stage 2 bid
offers.who: players with in_auction=true when two or more bid in stage 1
offers.options: The leader: 0 (hold at standing_bid) or every whole number from standing_bid+1 to their mice. Any other in_auction player: 0 (drop out) or every whole number from standing_bid+1 to their mice. If mice < standing_bid+1, only 0 is offered.

choices.why: The designer suggests 4, which is kept. 3 is the minimum for a sack built from several hidden cards with rivals bidding. Above 5 the sack and the bidding become too diluted for one card or bid to matter.

choices.what: Talk is a simultaneous poll broadcast to all
choices.why: The rules say messages are written simultaneously without seeing the others. Players disagree about the sack's value, so bluffing about one's own card matters.

choices.what: The tie-break uses the order (seat - start_seat - 1 + N) mod N
choices.why: This is the arithmetic form of 'first tied seat starting from the seat after start_seat'.
This encodes score first and cat_points as the tie-break. |cat_points| stays well below 500 given the finite cards.

choices.what: Card values are read from the card name (cat_X is worth X; rabbit and dogs are worth 0)
choices.why: The rules give cards as named tokens with these values.

choices.what: Players are offered only legal numbers, though the rules also say out-of-range numbers mean pass or drop out
choices.why: The engine offers ranges. The out-of-range rule is still stated so the resolution stays faithful.

simplifications.what: The branches 'round ends' and 'go to R10' are run as per-step `when` conditions on bidder_count and sack_winner in a flat step list
simplifications.why: The engine has no block branching. Single steps with arithmetic conditions give the same result.

simplifications.what: The dog rule and sack_value are worked out in one update step with conditional arithmetic over sack_cards
simplifications.why: The removal rules are deterministic arithmetic, so no referee is needed.
